land.text: Naples and its district, under local dukes since 661 ('obtained from the emperor Constans II the right to be ruled by a local duke') and nominally Byzantine until 763

predecessors.note: The infobox says 'Established: 600'. The Cliopatria row, and this dossier, start in 763 when Stephen II 'switched his allegiance from Constantinople to Rome'; the earlier duchy lies in the Byzantine Empire dossier.

land.text: Naples and its district, absorbed by Roger II

successors.note: 'Roger finally absorbed the Duchy of Naples into his new kingdom in 1139' (Sergius VII page); the Naples page's infobox gives annexation in 1137. Cliopatria's Duchy row ends 1138 and the Kingdom of Sicily row begins in 1139.

capitals.name: Naples
capitals.note: The duchy was the city of Naples and its district; no other seat is named on the pages opened.

keyframe_review.note: Stephen II took the duchy from Byzantine to papal suzerainty in 763. The shape is Naples and its district (1,035 km2; three cells). The page says 'Gaeta, Amalfi, and Sorrento took their independence from Naples in the early 9th century', so the duchy was larger before, but no extent is given: unverified: page budget. No infobox area.
Same district (+24 km2). 'In 840, Duke Sergius I made the succession to the duchy hereditary' (the infobox says 850); no territorial change is dated.

The shape loses its western cell (770 km2, two cells east of the city) in 960 and gains 96 km2 in 980-989; no page opened dates or explains either change, and Amalfi appears as its own Cliopatria row from 960 (Amalfi, Gaeta and Sorrento are said to have become independent in the early 9th century). Left as drawn: unverified: page budget.
866 km2 against 770 in the neighbouring shapes; unexplained by the pages opened (unverified: page budget).
Valid 990-1026; Pandulf IV of Capua (prince 1016-1022 and from 1026) 'defeated and deposed Sergius IV of Naples' in 1027.

correction.text: the Naples district as in 990, restored to Sergius IV in 1029

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1029-1033: Cliopatria has no Naples shape for 1028-1033 and gives the Naples cells to Capua. 'Sergius was reinstalled in 1029 by a Norman army under Rainulf', so the duchy is back by 1029; Capua held it 1027-1028.

The shape loses its western cells (722 km2; bbox from 14.26 E). The County of Aversa page dates the grant of Aversa to Rainulf to 1030 ('gave the town and vicinity of Aversa as a county to Ranulf') and the Naples page to 1027, but neither mentions the Pozzuoli-Cumae side; the Aversa cession is a ledger loss. Left as drawn.
The shape loses 24 km2 in 1085; no page dates it. The duchy otherwise stands unchanged under Norman suzerainty to 1131.

Cliopatria ends this shape in 1138. Sergius VII died at Rignano on 30 October 1137 but 'Roger finally absorbed the Duchy of Naples into his new kingdom in 1139' after the nobility acknowledged the young Alfonso of Hauteville as duke; the shape should run to 1139.

ledger.note: 763: Duke Stephen II turns Naples from Constantinople to Rome. 'In 763, the duke Stephen II switched his allegiance from Constantinople to Rome.' Local dukes date from 661; the infobox says 'Established: 600'.
840: the ducal succession becomes hereditary. 'In 840, Duke Sergius I made the succession to the duchy hereditary' (infobox: 850). Same state.

region.text: Naples, whose duke Sergius IV was deposed by Pandulf IV of Capua

ledger.note: 1027: Naples falls to Capua. 'In 1027, he defeated and deposed Sergius IV of Naples.' The page does not say Pandulf held the city; Cliopatria gives the Naples cells to Capua from 1028.
1029: Naples recovered. 'Sergius was reinstalled in 1029 by a Norman army under Rainulf.'

region.text: the town and vicinity of Aversa

ledger.note: 1030: Sergius IV gives Aversa to Rainulf. 'In 1030, the first Norman foothold in the Mezzogiorno was created' when the duke 'gave the town and vicinity of Aversa as a county to Ranulf'; the Naples page dates the gift to 1027. Cliopatria's Norman Italy row begins in 1034.

24 April 1135: Naples rises against Roger II. 'on 24 April 1135, a Pisan fleet under the exiled Robert of Capua laid anchor in Naples'; the rebels were besieged until spring 1136. Sergius had submitted to Roger in 1131 and done homage after the fall of Capua in 1134. [Reviewer eu-13-e, 2026-10-25: counterpart changed from norman-italy to kingdom-of-sicily: the norman-italy dossier ends in December 1130 with Roger II's coronation, and Sergius VII's page has Roger fighting Naples as king.]

1139: the fighting ends in annexation. Sergius VII died at Rignano on 30 October 1137; his death left no heir and Roger II 'finally absorbed the Duchy of Naples into his new kingdom in 1139'. [Reviewer eu-13-e, 2026-10-25: counterpart changed from norman-italy to kingdom-of-sicily: the norman-italy dossier ends in December 1130 with Roger II's coronation, and Sergius VII's page has Roger fighting Naples as king.]

region.text: Naples and its district, absorbed into the Kingdom of Sicily

ledger.note: 1139: Roger II absorbs Naples. 'Roger finally absorbed the Duchy of Naples into his new kingdom in 1139'; the Norman-conquest page: 'That year, Roger absorbed Naples into his kingdom.'
1139: the last Italian duchy of Byzantine origin ends. Cliopatria's last shape is 1138; the Naples page's infobox gives annexation in 1137.

wars.name: Pandulf IV's conquest of Naples
wars.outcome: Pandulf IV deposed Sergius IV in 1027; Rainulf's Normans reinstalled Sergius in 1029 and he granted them Aversa.
wars.note: The Naples page puts the Aversa grant in 1027.

wars.name: Battle of Ostia
wars.outcome: Naples' fleet fought the Arabs at the Battle of Ostia in 849; no territorial result.
wars.note: The page also says Naples asked the Arabs for help against a Lombard siege from Benevento in 836.

wars.name: Battle of the Garigliano
wars.outcome: Gregory IV and John II 'participated at the Battle of the Garigliano in 915'; no territorial result.

wars.name: Roger II's conquest of Naples
wars.outcome: Sergius VII submitted to Roger in 1131, did homage after the fall of Capua in 1134, joined the revolt of Robert II of Capua and Ranulf of Alife (Naples rose on 24 April 1135) and died at Rignano on 30 October 1137; Roger absorbed the duchy in 1139.
wars.note: Sources differ on the end: the Naples page gives surrender in 1137, the Sergius and Norman-conquest pages 1139.

certainty.note: A city-state of a few hundred square kilometres whose frontiers with Capua, Salerno and Aversa are not described on the pages opened; the coast is the only firm edge.

sources.title: Duchy of Naples
sources.note: Infobox (established 600, local duke 661), 763 switch to Rome, early-9th-century independence of Gaeta, Amalfi and Sorrento, 840 hereditary, 849, 915, 1027, 1137. No area.

sources.title: County of Aversa
sources.note: Aversa granted to Rainulf in 1030 by Sergius IV; 1058 Richard conquered Capua.

sources.title: Sergius VII of Naples
sources.note: Reign 1122-1137, 1131 submission, 1134 homage, 24 April 1135 revolt, Rignano 30 October 1137, absorption 1139.

sources.title: Pandulf IV of Capua
sources.note: Sergius IV deposed 1027, reinstalled 1029 by Rainulf.

sources.title: Norman conquest of southern Italy
sources.note: Aversa 1030, Naples and Roger II 1131-1139, last duke died 30 October 1137, absorbed 1139.

notes: Page budget (5) used. No page gives an infobox area, so the area comparison could not be made; Cliopatria's shape is two to three 253 km2 cells for the whole life. Unexplained Cliopatria changes: the loss of the western cell in 960, +96 km2 in 980-989, the western cells lost by 1034 (Cuma-Pozzuoli side) and -24 km2 in 1085; the pages opened date none of them. The early extent of the duchy (Gaeta, Amalfi and Sorrento independent only in the early 9th century, no year) is not drawn: Cliopatria's 763 shape is the Naples district only, so a gap-filler should open 'Gaeta', 'Duchy of Amalfi' and 'Sorrento' pages to date the three secessions. Cliopatria gives the Naples cells to Capua 1028-1033; the pages say Sergius IV was back in 1029. The Aversa grant is 1030 on two pages and 1027 on the Naples page. Guaimar IV of Salerno held Naples at some point ('dominion ... over Salerno, Amalfi, Gaeta, Naples, Sorrento') but the page gives no year, so no event. Annexation: 1139 on the Sergius VII and Norman-conquest pages, 1137 in the Naples infobox; the dossier ends 1139, Cliopatria 1138. Counterparts needing dossiers: Duchy of Gaeta (not in Cliopatria), County of Aversa (inside norman-italy). Rulers omitted: no page opened lists the dukes with reign years.
